title: Register the worker on a claim-less prepare of an owned cell
description: In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/prepare.rs run_dispatch_prepare: when --kind cell and --claim is absent, after check_cell_claim_ownership confirms the cell is claimed by --worker, call crate::verbs::state_group::register_worker_for_cell(root, worker, cell_id, cell tier) exactly as claim_and_reserve_for_dispatch does (prepare.rs ~1300-1309), splice worker_registered / registration_error into the payload envelope the same way (~1547-1550), and never fail the prepare on a registration error. Ownership refusal still registers nothing; non-cell kinds unchanged; the probe/first pass must not double-register (upsert makes a repeat harmless).
action: Add the branch in run_dispatch_prepare; add tests in verbs/drivers/tests.rs next to claim_less_prepare_registers_no_worker (tests.rs ~2219): (a) claim-less prepare of a cell owned by --worker registers the row findable by registered_worker_for_cell, (b) claim-less prepare of a cell owned by another worker refuses and registers nothing, (c) an unclaimed cell with no --claim keeps the existing behaviour. Update the sentence in skills/bee-swarming/references/swarming-reference.md ~163-169 that says registration happens only under --claim, and the matching line in docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md if it states the same; then run the regen chain (bee dev regen) and bee dev release-manifest --check inside this cell.
verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee drivers:: — green; bee dev release-manifest --check

trace.outcome: Claim-less dispatch prepare registers the worker on a cell it already owns
deviations: Worker ran as a standalone herding executor and could not run bee commands; the orchestrator ran bee dev regen and release-manifest --check in the worktree afterwards and committed the rendered trees in a second commit
Knowledge line updated in docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/cells-completion-judge-and-archive.md rather than dispatch.md, where the registration rule actually lived
